analysis.label: 替换

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 张冠李戴 It would give him more time to be with his loved ones 来自女方 giving us an opportunity to spend more time with our loved ones，那是女方反驳时说的合住好处， 不是男方的看法，主体说反了。 借用原文：giving us an opportunity to spend more time with our loved ones B) 张冠李戴 It would be good for those who value relationships 对应女方观点 if we value relationships, sharing a home isn't depriving ourselves of space，仍是女方的论调而非 男方所说，归属错位。 借用原文：if we value relationships, sharing a home isn't depriving ourselves of space D) 原词陷阱 It would deprive him of his individuality 蹭了女方原文 sharing a home isn't depriving ourselves of space 的 depriving，但原文说的是「不会剥夺空间」且是女方所言，D 既盗 词又把否定说成肯定、还安到男方头上。 借用原文：sharing a home isn't depriving ourselves of space 1 W: Thank you for inviting me to the gallery, Christopher. I haven't visited here since your predecessor's retirement function. W: 谢谢你邀请我来画廊,Christopher。自从你前任的退休招待会之后我就没来过这里了。 2 M: Would you like to see the newest additions to our collection first, Catherine? M: 你想先看看我们馆藏的最新藏品吗,Catherine? 3 W: Are those the landscapes by Danielle Gregory? I absolutely adore her work. W: 是Danielle Gregory的那些风景画吗?我特别喜欢她的作品。 4 M: This first piece was a gift to the gallery from the artist herself, and it's quite exquisite. M: 第一幅作品是艺术家本人赠送给画廊的,非常精美。 5 W: I love how she depicts the barren landscape. The colors complement each other perfectly. W: 我喜欢她描绘荒凉景色的方式。色彩搭配得非常完美。 6 M: You can sense the desolation in the picture. This piece was inspired by Gregory's recent trek in the Gobi Desert. M: 你能从画中感受到那种荒凉。这幅作品的灵感来自Gregory最近的戈壁沙漠之旅。 7 W: And how did you obtain her other piece over here? W: 那你们是怎么得到她这边的另一幅作品的? 8 M: It was purchased at auction by an anonymous collector who lent it to the gallery for display. This composition is one of her most acclaimed paintings. M: 是一位匿名收藏家在拍卖会上购买的,然后借给画廊展出。这幅是她最受赞誉的画作之一。 Questions 5 to 8 are based on the conversation you have just heard. 9 W: It must have cost that collector a small fortune to purchase this. W: 那位收藏家买这幅画肯定花了一大笔钱。 10 M: Obviously, I can't disclose the exact amount he paid, but it was substantial. M: 显然我不能透露他支付的具体金额,但确实很可观。 11 W: There's so much detail in this painting. I feel like I can really immerse myself in the scene. I particularly like the symmetry created by the reflection of the mountain in the lake. W: 这幅画有太多细节了。我感觉自己真的能沉浸在这个场景中。我特别喜欢山在湖中的倒影所形成的对 称感。 12 M: This particular piece was the one that was nominated for a Gateway Award. I was lucky enough to attend the award ceremony as Gregory's guest. M: 这幅作品就是被提名Gateway Award的那幅。我很幸运能作为Gregory的客人参加了颁奖典礼。 13 W: So you know her personally. I assume she's an eccentric artist. W: 所以你和她私下认识。我猜她是个很古怪的艺术家吧。 14 M: Quite the opposite. In fact, she's not at all eccentric. I would say she's one of the most easygoing and intelligent people I know. M: 恰恰相反。事实上,她一点都不古怪。我觉得她是我认识的人中最随和、最聪明的人之一。 15 W: I'd love to be able to meet her. There are so many questions I'd like to ask. W: 我很想见见她。我有好多问题想问。 16 M: What a coincidence! I'm meeting her for dinner tonight. Would you like to come along? M: 真巧!我今晚要和她一起吃晚饭。你想一起来吗? 17 W: I'd love to. Thank you. W: 我很乐意。谢谢你。

Forgiveness doesn't mean reconciliation. We don't have to return to the same relationship, nor do we have to accept the same harmful behaviors from an offender. Forgiveness is vitally important for the mental health of certain victims. It propels people forward rather than keeping them emotionally engaged in an injustice or trauma. Carrying the hurt or anger of an offense leads the body to release stress chemicals. Eliminating the perpetual flow of those chemicals may also explain why forgiveness provides physical health benefits. 宽恕是释放怨恨或愤怒。宽恕并不意味着和解。我们不必回到原来的关系中,也不必接受冒犯者同样的有害 行为。宽恕对某些受害者的心理健康至关重要。它推动人们向前迈进,而不是让他们在情感上纠缠于不公或 创伤之中。携带冒犯带来的伤害或愤怒会导致身体释放应激化学物质。消除这些化学物质的持续流动也可 以解释为什么宽恕能带来身体健康方面的益处。 2 There are scenarios in which forgiveness is not the best course. Sometimes the victim becomes more empowered when they give themselves permission not to forgive. Forgiveness can be challenging. This is especially true when the offending party offers an insincere apology, or maybe they haven't offered anything at all. However, it's often the healthiest path forward. It's important to cultivate forgiveness by developing compassion for the offender, reflect on whether the act was due to malicious intent, or whether it was caused by challenging circumstances in the offender's life. 在某些情况下,宽恕并不是最佳选择。有时当受害者允许自己不去宽恕时,他们会变得更有力量。宽恕可能 具有挑战性。当冒犯方提供一个不真诚的道歉,或者他们根本没有提供任何道歉时,情况尤其如此。然而,这 通常是最健康的前进之路。重要的是通过对冒犯者培养同情心来培养宽恕,反思该行为是由于恶意还是由于 冒犯者生活中的困难处境所导致。 Questions 9 to 11 are based on the passage you have just heard. 3 What about forgiving ourselves? We sometimes need to take responsibility for mistakes, but intense guilt and shame aren't a desirable outcome in the long run. Forgiving yourself may seem like an ambiguous process. You can begin by acknowledging that you are at fault, taking responsibility for the hurt you caused, then reflecting on why the event occurred. questions.stem: When is forgiveness especially challenging?

analysis.label: 定位

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: reflect on whether the act was due to malicious intent, or whether it was caused by challenging circumstances in the offender's life ↔Find out why he committed the offense '反思动机是恶意还是处境'=弄清原因

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 未提及 Talk with the offender calmly. 听上去是化解冲突的好办法，但录音讲的方法是'对冒犯者 培养同情、反思其动机'，从没提'与对方平静交谈(talk with…calmly)'，属合理却未提及的 脑补做法。 B) 原词陷阱 Accept the offender's apology. 借了录音里的 apology 一词，但原文 the offending party offers an insincere apology, or maybe they haven't offered anything at all 说的 是道歉往往不真诚甚至没有道歉，宽恕并不以'接受道歉'为前提，选项与文意相悖。 借用原文：This is especially true when the offending party offers an insincere apology, or maybe they haven't offered anything at all. D) 原词陷阱 Determine how serious the offense was. 借了录音里反复出现的 offense，但原文要人反 思的是冒犯的'原因(why/intent)'，不是冒犯的'严重程度(how serious)'，偷换了反思的对 象。 借用原文：reflect on whether the act was due to malicious intent, or whether it was caused by challenging circumstances in the offender's life 1 The Glasgow subway first opened in 1896 as a cable-hauled system. It is generally recognised as the world's third underground railway, after London and Budapest. In its long history, it has never been expanded, remaining as a single loop line with a mere 15 stations. At its peak, it served the shipyard workers on the south side of the city. In the 1960s, there was a decline in the shipbuilding industry and the popularity of private transport grew. As a result, the subway saw a rapid decline in ridership. Glasgow地铁于1896年首次开通，采用缆索牵引系统。它被公认为世界第三条地下铁路，仅次于伦敦和 布达佩斯。在其悠久的历史中，它从未扩建过，始终保持为单一环线，仅有15个站点。在其鼎盛时期，它 为城市南部的造船厂工人提供服务。20世纪60年代，造船业衰退，私人交通工具日益普及。因此,地铁的 客流量迅速下降。 2 It ran with little further change until 1977 when its new operators closed it for major modernisation investment. Carriages were replaced, ventilation was improved, and the main depot was also renovated and fitted with connecting tracks to replace the outdated crane transfer mechanism. The subway in its present form reopened for operation in April 1980. Since its relaunch, the subway has seen a revival in its fortunes. It serves as a viable alternative to other forms of transport and has gone a long way to alleviate traffic jams in the city centre. In 1996, the system reached an important milestone—100 years. To commemorate this special event, the colour scheme of the train carriages was updated. 它在运营中几乎没有进一步的变化，直到1977年其新运营商关闭地铁进行重大现代化改造投资。车厢被 更换，通风得到改善，主车辆段也进行了翻新并安装了连接轨道以取代过时的起重机转运机制。地铁以其 现有形式于1980年4月重新开放运营。自重新启用以来，地铁的命运得到了复兴。它作为其他交通方式的 可行替代方案，在很大程度上缓解了市中心的交通拥堵。1996年，该系统达到了一个重要的里程碑—— 100周年。为纪念这一特殊事件，列车车厢的配色方案得到了更新。 Questions 12 to 15 are based on the passage you have just heard. 3 Recently, high-tech systems such as smart card ticketing machines and smart gates are used across all subway stations. The smart card provides more convenient travel, and passengers simply top up their cards and tap them to get in and out the subway. Since its launch, the technology has been adopted by more than 100,000 subway customers. 近期，智能卡售票机和智能闸机等高科技系统在所有地铁站投入使用。智能卡提供了更便捷的出行方式， 乘客只需为卡充值并刷卡即可进出地铁。自推出以来，该技术已被超过10万名地铁乘客采用。

questions.stem: What does the passage say about the Glasgow subway in the 1960s?

questions.answerText: The number of passengers dropped sharply.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: In the 1960s, there was a decline in the shipbuilding industry and the popularity of private transport grew. As a result, the subway saw a rapid decline in ridership. 在 20 世纪 60 年代，造船业衰退、私人交通工具日益普及。结果，地铁的客流量急剧 下降。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 时间词 + 因果信号 As a result。听到 In the 1960s 锁定时间，再抓住因果信号 As a result，结果句 the subway saw a rapid decline in ridership 才是承载答案的落点——这 是篇章题靠因果结论句定位的典型。

analysis.text: B) 与原文相反 It served more and more commuters. 把方向反了——原文 1960 年代是 a rapid decline in ridership（客流骤降），B 却说服务越来越多通勤者，正好相反。"客流增多" 是 录音里别的时期（早年高峰）的情形，被挪到 1960 年代头上。 借用原文：a rapid decline in ridership C) 未提及 The number of stations increased to 50. 凭空捏造。原文明说 it has never been expanded, remaining as a single loop line with a mere 15 stations，站数一直是 15 且 从未扩建，根本没有增到 50 一说。 D) 原词陷阱 It became the longest in the United Kingdom. 借 "最长" 这类醒目说法制造诱惑，但原 文谈的是它是 the world's third underground railway（世界第三条地下铁），讲的是 "第 三早" 而非 "全英最长"，把 "第三" 偷换成 "最长"、把 "世界范围的早" 偷换成 "英国范围的 长"。 借用原文：the world's third underground railway, after London and Budapest

analysis.label: 定位

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 目的信号 for + 时间词 1977。听到 until 1977 锁定时间后，紧跟的介词 for major modernisation investment 里的 for 正是表目的的信号词，for 后面的成分就是关闭的 原因。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: for major modernisation investment ↔To have its systems modernised 同根词改写：modernisation→modernised，名词转动词被动

analysis.text: A) 未提及 To increase capacity to meet growing needs. 录音没有依据。原文反而强调它 has never been expanded（从未扩建），与 "增加运力" 相悖，更没说是为应对需求增长而关闭。 B) 未提及 To make way for other means of transport. 是无中生有。原文后文只说改造后地铁成了 a viable alternative to other forms of transport（其他交通的替代选择），是 "地铁替代 别的交通"，绝非 "为别的交通让路"，B 把关系搞反且与 1977 关闭目的无关。 借用原文：a viable alternative to other forms of transport D) 原词陷阱 To avoid further financial losses. 听感上呼应了前文客流下降，像是 "亏损"，但原文从未 把关闭归因于避免财务亏损，1977 关闭明确是 for major modernisation investment。它 借第一段衰退的语境制造 "亏损" 联想，属过度推断式的原词陷阱。 借用原文：a rapid decline in ridership

analysis.text: A) 未提及 They are usually crowded. 录音从未提到车站拥挤，是无中生有。原文末段讲的是高科技 系统，与拥挤无关。 C) 原词陷阱 They accept smartcards only. 盗用原文 smart card ticketing machines 的 smart card，但原文只说智能卡是高科技系统之一、很方便，从未说车站 "只收" 智能卡。only 是 凭空加的绝对范围词，把 "用了智能卡" 偷改成 "只收智能卡"。 借用原文：smart card ticketing machines and smart gates D) 张冠李戴 They are colourfully decorated. 借了原文 the colour scheme of the train carriages was updated 的 colour 字眼，但那是为纪念百年更新了"车厢"的配色，对象是 train carriages，且属 1996 年的旧事，并非如今 "所有车站" 装饰艳丽，对象和时间都被张冠李 戴。 借用原文：the colour scheme of the train carriages was updated Section C 1 If you visit the Great Smoky Mountains National Park, chances are you will remember the roadside or campground bears above all else. Bears are the most popular animals in a number of our national parks. In these mountains, where the population of bears runs into the hundreds, opportunities to observe these large wild animals are plentiful during the summer. 如果你访问大烟山国家公园,你很可能会对路边或营地的熊印象最为深刻。熊是我们许多国家公园中最受欢 迎的动物。在这些山区,熊的数量达到数百只,夏季有充足的机会观察这些大型野生动物。 2 Since national parks are wildlife sanctuaries where no disturbance of the native animals is allowed, years of protection have served to break down the wild bears' fear of humans. Now, instead of depending on their own resources for a living, many bears patrol park roads and campgrounds. They give the garbage cans a frequent going over. An occasional offer of food from a park visitor, an illegal and dangerous practice, makes beggars of them. Bears are very often hungry and since they will feed on almost any kind of plant or animal, garbage is quite acceptable. 由于国家公园是野生动物保护区,不允许对本地动物进行任何干扰,多年的保护已经消除了野熊对人类的恐 惧。现在,许多熊不再依靠自己的能力谋生,而是在公园道路和营地巡游。它们经常翻找垃圾桶。游客偶尔 提供的食物——这是一种违法且危险的行为——使它们变成了乞讨者。熊经常很饿,由于它们几乎以任何 种类的植物或动物为食,垃圾是完全可以接受的。 Questions 16 to 18 are based on the recording you have just heard. 3 Feeding them, however, represents misguided kindness because the bears come to expect such generosity from everyone and consequently, trouble could lie ahead. Park rules prohibit the feeding of bears. Violators are arrested. Every year, doctors who have offices near the park treat a number of cases of bear bites and bear scratches. Some of the accidents have come about in strange ways. 然而,喂食它们代表着错误的善意,因为熊会期待每个人都如此慷慨,因此可能会带来麻烦。公园规定禁止喂 熊。违反者将被逮捕。每年,在公园附近开诊所的医生都会治疗一些熊咬伤和熊抓伤的病例。一些事故以奇 怪的方式发生。 4 One man was in the process of feeding two small cubs, when the mother bear appeared and insisted upon having some of the food. Shoving the big bear aside with one hand, the man continued feeding the cubs when suddenly he was struck a fierce blow in the face. C) At best this can be termed "the extinction of experience," where our cultural and natural histories fade from our memories and therefore our reality. At its worst it becomes something even more concerning: "biophobia," the fear of living things and a complete aversion to nature.
D) This isn't the fiction of living in a cold, empty dystopia(绝望的世界). Sadly, it's becoming a way of life for too many people—especially children. A recent study in Japan paints a striking portrait of this problem. A survey of more than 5,300 school children in the Tochigi Prefecture examined their perception of 14 local insect species and one spider. The results? A collective "ew!" Most of the students saw the species as things to dislike or fear, or even as sources of danger. The less experience the students had with nature, the more negative their feelings.

Lead researcher Masashi Soga with the University of Tokyo says the study stemmed from observations about today's nature-deficient children. "Humans inherently avoid dangerous organisms such as bees, but children these days avoid even harmless insects such as butterflies and dragonflies(蜻蜓)," he says. "I have long wondered why so many of today's children react like this."

In fact, these parental emotions were strong enough to overwhelm any positive experiences the children might have gained from direct experiences in nature. As Soga and his coauthors wrote in their paper, "Our results suggest that there is likely a feedback loop in which an increase in people who have negative attitudes towards nature in one generation will lead to a further increase in people with similar attitudes in the next generation."

The politician who votes against wildlife protection because she's never seen a wolf in the wild. The corporation that wants to bulldoze(用推土机推平) the habitat of a rare frog.

blocks.label: C
blocks.text: At best this can be termed "the extinction of experience," where our cultural and natural histories fade from our memories and therefore our reality. At its worst it becomes something even more concerning: "biophobia," the fear of living things and a complete aversion to nature.

blocks.label: D
blocks.text: This isn't the fiction of living in a cold, empty dystopia(绝望的世界). Sadly, it's becoming a way of life for too many people—especially children. A recent study in Japan paints a striking portrait of this problem. A survey of more than 5,300 school children in the Tochigi Prefecture examined their perception of 14 local insect species and one spider. The results? A collective "ew!" Most of the students saw the species as things to dislike or fear, or even as sources of danger. The less experience the students had with nature, the more negative their feelings.

blocks.label: E
blocks.text: The results were published earlier this year in the journal Biological Conservation. Lead researcher Masashi Soga with the University of Tokyo says the study stemmed from observations about today's nature-deficient children. "Humans inherently avoid dangerous organisms such as bees, but children these days avoid even harmless insects such as butterflies and dragonflies(蜻蜓)," he says. "I have long wondered why so many of today's children react like this."

blocks.label: F
blocks.text: Although the children's reactions were somewhat expected, the new study did contain an unexpected finding: Many of the surveyed children revealed that their parents also expressed fear or disgust of the same animals. In fact, these parental emotions were strong enough to overwhelm any positive experiences the children might have gained from direct experiences in nature. As Soga and his coauthors wrote in their paper, "Our results suggest that there is likely a feedback loop in which an increase in people who have negative attitudes towards nature in one generation will lead to a further increase in people with similar attitudes in the next generation."

blocks.label: G
blocks.text: And that's possibly the greater threat posed by extinction of experience. Soga suggests the generational loss—condition previously dubbed environmental generational amnesia(遗忘)—could chip away at our societal ability to preserve what we're losing. "I believe that increased biophobia is a major, but invisible, threat to global biodiversity," Soga says. "As the number of children who have biophobia increases, public interest and support for biodiversity conservation will gradually decline. Although many conservation biologists still consider that preventing the loss of wildlife habitat is the most important way to conserve biodiversity, I think preventing increased biophobia is also important for conservation."

blocks.label: H
blocks.text: What's to be done about this? The paper makes several recommendations, the most obvious of which is that children should experience nature more often. The authors also suggest establishing policies to guide these natural experiences and increasing educational programs about the natural world.

blocks.label: I
blocks.text: Helping parents to see species around them in a new light would make a difference, too. And, of course, maintaining support for preserving the wild spaces where these "scary" creatures live is the most important thing of all. That's a point reinforced by another recent study, which found that wild spaces located within urban areas—and the plants and animals that thrive in them—are particularly important for human health and well-being.

blocks.label: J
blocks.text: Published in the journal Frontiers in Sustainable Cities, the study examined attitudes toward Discovery Park, the heavily forested 534-acre public park in Seattle, Washington. It found that the public had the most appreciation for—and gained the most value from—the wildest parts of the park. "I have seen whales, seals, fish, eagles, shorebirds and many other sea creatures in their natural habitat," one survey participant wrote. "Coming here with people has allowed me to connect and talk with them about conversation that simply does not happen in everyday life," wrote another.

blocks.label: K
blocks.text: The participants reported that their most valuable experiences in the park included encountering wildlife, walking through open spaces, exploring the beach and finding beautiful views. "We saw that a large majority of participants' interactions, especially their most meaningful interactions, depended on Discovery Park's relative wildness," says lead author Elizabeth Lev, a master's student in the University of Washington's Human Interaction with Nature Lab. This is only possible because the park is relatively wild. After all, you can't enjoy watching birds if there are no birds to follow, gaze at the sunset if it's obscured by skyscrapers, or stop and smell the flowers if they don't have room to grow.

blocks.label: L
blocks.text: And yet even this long-protected space could someday become less hospitable to nature. Over the past few years a lot of people and organizations have suggested developing parts of Discovery Park or the neighboring area. Most recently a plan proposed building 34 acres of much-needed affordable housing and parking spaces adjacent to the park, bringing with them noise, traffic and pollution.

blocks.label: M
blocks.text: If anything like that happened, both the park and the people of Seattle could lose something vital. And that would continue the trend of chipping away at Seattle's—and the world's—natural spaces, leaving just tiny pocket parks and green-but-empty spaces that offer little real value to wildlife, plants or people. N) "It is true that any interaction with nature is better than none, but I don't want people to be satisfied with any small bit of grass and trees," Lev says. "We have been in this cycle of environmental generational amnesia for a long time, where the baseline keeps shifting and we don't even realize what we're losing until it's gone. If we can get people to understand how much meaning and value can come from having more experiences with more wild forms of nature, then maybe we can stop this cycle and move toward conserving and restoring what we have left." O) Building this understanding in an ever-more fearful and disconnected world may be the biggest challenge. P1 If there's one rule that most parents cling to in the confusing, fast-changing world of kids and media, it's "No screens before age 2."

P2 As of today, that rule has been thrown out the window.

P3 The American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP), which first issued that recommendation back in 1999, has extensively updated and revised its guidelines for children and adolescents to reflect new research and new habits.

P4 The new guidelines, especially for very young children, shift the focus from WHAT is on the screen to WHO else is in the room. And in doing so, they raise some intriguing points about the future of learning from media. Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage.

P5 For babies younger than 18 months, AAP still says no screens at all are the best idea—with one notable exception: Live video chat. Surveys indicate that families already popularly believe that "Face time doesn't count", or at least that the benefit of virtual visits with grandparents or other relatives outweighs the potential cost of exposing babies to the laptop or smartphone.

P6 The AAP doesn't cite positive evidence that infants actually get something out of this kind of "conversation", the way that they clearly do from live social interaction. But there's some observational research that infants as young as six months old are emotionally engaged by playing live peekaboo(躲猫 猫) with Grandma online.

P7 For infants and toddlers(学步儿童), ages 15 months to 2 years old, there's limited evidence from a couple of very small studies that they can learn new words from educational media, if and only if parents are watching alongside them, repeating what the video says and/or drawing attention to what is on the screen. In other words, treating a video or an app like a picture book is the best bet.

P8 The flip side of this is that many studies have actually shown poorer language skills correlated with earlier solo viewing of "educational" videos. There's also research that shows language delays in children who watch more TV and start watching earlier. In both cases, the problem seems to be media replacing interaction with people. For this reason, the new AAP guideline has changed from "avoid all screens under age 2" to "avoid solo media use in this age group."

P9 For preschoolers ages 2 to 5, there's more evidence that they have the ability to transfer knowledge from screens to the real world, including early literacy and math. For this age group, AAP recommends no more than an hour a day of screen use. And, just as with younger children, they want care-givers to take part in screen time: "Co-view with your children, help children understand what they are seeing, and help them apply what they learn to the world around them."

writing.model: In an era of information explosion, it is vitally important to develop the ability to think critically and make rational choices. Every day we are flooded with news, advertisements and social-media posts, yet not all of them are trustworthy. Only those who can sift truth from falsehood are able to stay clear-headed. There are two compelling reasons why this ability matters. First, information today is a mixture of facts and rumours, and a careless reader can easily be misled. Take online rumours during public emergencies for example: people who forward them without checking often spread panic. Second, the cost of a wrong choice has risen sharply; whether we are selecting a course, a product or a career, rational judgement based on reliable evidence saves us from regret. Therefore, we should never swallow information passively. By questioning the source, comparing different views and weighing the evidence before us, we can turn the endless flood of information into a real advantage rather than a heavy burden. In the end, critical thinking is not an optional skill but a survival tool for the modern mind.

sentences.text: 本句为简单判断句无需重构 本句结构简单，就是一个「主语 + is + one of the + 复数名词 + of 短语」的判断句，不含多余动 词或长修饰，直接照主干译出即可，无需降级处理。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 陈述至今仍成立的事实（它现在依然是发祥地之一），用一般现在时 is。 单复数 「之一」决定 birthplaces 用复数；one of the 后面必须接复数名词。 用词 「发祥地」可用 birthplaces 或 cradles，与 globalPlan 选定的一致即可；「中华民族」用 the Chinese nation。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: The Loess Plateau is one of the birthplaces of the Chinese nation. 4. 早在5500年前，人们就已经在黄土高原上开始农耕。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 人们开始农耕（主语策略：原句主语） 中文主语是泛指的 人们，英文用 people 承接。主干是 people began farming（人们开始农 耕），早在5500年前 是时间状语，在黄土高原上 是地点状语，都挂在主干外。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 时间地点状语前后安放 「早在5500年前」译为时间状语 as early as 5,500 years ago，可放句首；「在黄土高原上」译为 地点状语 on the Loess Plateau，放谓语之后。主干 began farming 不变，两个状语分别安放， 无需从句。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 这是讲5500年前已发生的历史动作，必须偏离全篇现在时基调，改用一般过去时 began；「就已 经开始」强调那时已经开始，也可用过去完成时 had already begun 更精确。这是本篇最关键的 时态切换点。 时间表达 「早在5500年前」用 as early as 5,500 years ago，as early as 正好对应「早在」的强调语气。 用词 「农耕」用 farming 或 agriculture／to farm；began farming 或 started farming 均可。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: As early as 5,500 years ago, people had already begun farming on the Loess Plateau. 5. 随着农耕业的持续发展，黄土高原人口不断增加，在秦汉时期就成为中国的政治和经济 中心。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 人口增加、(高原)成为中心（主语策略：原句主语） 本句有两个分句：前一分句主语是 黄土高原人口（its population），谓语「不断增加」grew； 后一分句 在秦汉时期就成为中国的政治和经济中心 的主语其实回到「黄土高原」（the region ／it），谓语「成为」became。要看清这里主语发生了切换：增加的是人口，成为中心的是高原 本身。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 随着用With短语、两动作分置 随着农耕业的持续发展 用 With the continuous development of farming 介词短语作伴随状语 开头；「人口不断增加」与「成为中心」是两个先后动作，可用 and 连接两个过去式谓语 its population grew and it became...，或把前者降级、后者作主干。秦汉时期作时间状语 during the Qin and Han dynasties。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 本句讲秦汉时期的历史进程，用一般过去时：grew、became，与上一句的过去时保持一致，不可 写成现在时。 主谓一致 population 作主语视为单数，谓语 grew（过去式不显数，但若用现在时须 grows）；it became 主谓相配。 名词化 「农耕业的持续发展」名词化为 the continuous development of farming，development 不可 数、前加 the 特指。 用词 「政治和经济中心」译 the political and economic center of China，center 单数（一个中心， 政治、经济共用），两个形容词并列修饰。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: With the continuous development of farming, its population kept growing, and during the Qin and Han dynasties it became the political and economic center of China. 6. 如今，随着西部大开发战略的实施，黄土高原地区的经济得到了迅速发展。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 经济得到迅速发展（主语策略：原句主语） 中文主语是 黄土高原地区的经济（the economy of the Loess Plateau region），谓语「得到了 迅速发展」。可处理为主动 has developed rapidly，主语就是 the economy；「得到了发展」是 中文常见的「得到 + 动词」结构，英文直接用动词 develop 即可，不必死扣「得到」译成 get。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 如今作时间状语、随着作伴随状语 如今 译 Today／Nowadays 放句首作时间状语；随着西部大开发战略的实施 同样用 With the implementation of the Western Development Strategy 介词短语作伴随状语；主干 the economy of the region has developed rapidly。两个状语前置，主句留核心动作。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 「如今……得到了迅速发展」讲的是从过去延续到现在的结果，用现在完成时 has developed 最贴 切（呼应「如今」的现时结果）；也可用一般现在时 develops。注意这里时态又切回了「现 在」，与第4、5句的历史过去时区分开。 主谓一致 主语 the economy 是单数，谓语 has developed 用第三人称单数 has。 名词化与冠词 「西部大开发战略的实施」名词化为 the implementation of the Western Development Strategy，implementation 前加 the 特指；战略名按 glossary 统一大写。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: Today, with the implementation of the Western Development Strategy, the economy of the Loess Plateau region has developed rapidly. 英语六级 2022年12月·第2套 · 全卷构成 Part III Part III Part III Part III
